package.title: 100 MDCAT-Style Genetics and Inheritance MCQs with Explanations

questions.question: Which term describes different versions of the same gene at a particular locus?
An organism with two identical alleles for a gene is described as:
If allele A is completely dominant to allele a, which genotype is heterozygous?
For a gene with complete dominance, which genotypes show the recessive phenotype?
A cross is written as Aa × Aa. Which gametes can each parent produce?
In the cross Aa × Aa, what fraction of offspring is expected to be aa?
In the cross Aa × Aa with complete dominance, what fraction is expected to show the dominant phenotype?
A test cross for an individual showing a dominant phenotype uses which partner genotype?
choices: Any genotype with a dominant allele

questions.question: An organism of unknown genotype with a dominant phenotype is crossed with aa. Half the offspring are recessive. What is the unknown genotype?
In a cross between Aa and aa, assuming complete dominance, what fraction of offspring is expected to show the dominant phenotype?
A plant with genotype Tt is self-crossed. If T is completely dominant, what is the expected phenotype ratio?
For a monohybrid cross Aa × Aa, what is the expected genotype ratio?
A cross Aa × aa produces offspring. What is the probability that one offspring will be heterozygous?
In a cross Aa × Aa, what is the probability that two successive offspring are both aa, assuming independent outcomes?
In a cross Aa × Aa, what is the probability that two offspring are both dominant-phenotype individuals, assuming independent outcomes?
For two independently assorting genes, what gametes can an AaBb individual produce?
In the cross AaBb × aabb, assume the genes assort independently. What fraction of offspring is expected to be aabb?
In AaBb × AaBb, with independent assortment and complete dominance at both loci, what fraction is expected to be dominant for A and recessive for b?
In AaBb × AaBb, assuming independent assortment and complete dominance, what fraction is expected to show both recessive phenotypes?
A cross AaBb × aabb is performed with independent assortment. What fraction of offspring is expected to show the dominant phenotype for both genes?
Which statement best describes independent assortment in a standard Mendelian model?
choices: Alleles of one gene always stay together
Alleles of different genes assort independently when the genes are unlinked
Dominant alleles are more likely to enter gametes

questions.question: Which cells are produced by meiosis from one diploid precursor cell, before considering later developmental changes?
A diploid species has 2n = 12 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are expected in each normal gamete?
During which stage of meiosis do homologous chromosomes separate?
Crossing over between homologous chromosomes usually occurs during which stage?
Which process most directly creates new combinations of alleles on chromosomes during meiosis?
An organism with genotype Aa forms gametes. Which principle explains why each gamete receives only one of the two alleles?
A gene's locus is best defined as:
choices: Its physical position on a chromosome
The shape of its protein product
The number of alleles in a population
The process of making a gamete

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes genotype from phenotype?
choices: Genotype is the allele combination; phenotype is an observable or measurable trait
Genotype is an organism's habitat; phenotype is its chromosome number
They mean exactly the same thing
Phenotype always reveals the complete genotype

questions.question: In incomplete dominance, a heterozygote typically has a phenotype:
choices: Determined only by the father's allele

questions.question: In codominance, a heterozygote typically:
choices: Has an intermediate blend in every case

questions.question: The human ABO blood group is an example involving:
choices: One allele with incomplete dominance only

questions.question: Which genotype produces blood group AB in the ABO system?
A parent with genotype IAi and a parent with genotype IBi have a child. Which blood-group phenotype is possible?
A parent with blood group O has genotype ii. The other parent has genotype IAIB. Which blood groups can their children have?
If both parents have genotype ii for the ABO system, what blood-group phenotype is expected in their children?
A red-green colour-vision trait is treated as X-linked recessive. A carrier mother (XᴺXⁿ) and an unaffected father (XᴺY) have a son. What is the probability that the son is affected?
For an X-linked recessive trait, an affected father and a non-carrier mother have a daughter. What is the daughter's expected status?
choices: She cannot inherit the father's allele

questions.question: For an X-linked recessive trait, an affected mother (XⁿXⁿ) and an unaffected father (XᴺY) have children. What is expected for their sons?
choices: No sons can inherit the trait

questions.question: A father passes his X chromosome directly to which children?
A gene located on the Y chromosome is ordinarily transmitted from an affected father to:

A trait is observed in each generation, affects males and females similarly, and an affected heterozygous parent can pass it to a child of either sex. Which pattern is most consistent with these clues?
Two unaffected parents have a child with a rare autosomal recessive trait. Under a simple single-gene model, what is the most likely genotype of each parent?
Under a simple autosomal recessive model, what is the chance that an unaffected sibling of an affected child from two carrier parents is a carrier?
An affected individual with an autosomal recessive condition has genotype aa. If the other parent is confirmed AA, what genotypes are expected among their children?
An autosomal dominant trait is caused by allele D. A heterozygous affected parent (Dd) and an unaffected parent (dd) have a child. What is the probability the child is affected?
In a typical pedigree, which observation most strongly supports mitochondrial inheritance?
choices: Affected fathers transmit the trait to all daughters
Affected mothers can transmit the trait to children of either sex
The trait skips every other generation

questions.question: A person has two alleles of a gene on a pair of homologous autosomes. One allele was inherited from each parent. This illustrates:
Which structure is the main hereditary material in most living organisms?
A DNA nucleotide contains which three components?
choices: Deoxyribose, phosphate, and a nitrogenous base

questions.question: Which base pairs with adenine in double-stranded DNA?
Which base pairs with cytosine in DNA?
If a double-stranded DNA molecule contains 30% adenine, what percentage is guanine?
A DNA strand has the base sequence 5′-A G T C-3′. What is the complementary strand written antiparallel?
In the double helix, the two DNA strands are described as antiparallel because they:
choices: Contain exactly the same bases in the same order

questions.question: DNA replication is called semiconservative because each daughter DNA molecule contains:
choices: One parental strand and one newly synthesized strand
One DNA strand and one RNA strand

questions.question: Which enzyme unwinds the DNA double helix at a replication fork?
Which enzyme joins adjacent DNA fragments on the lagging strand?
Why is one new DNA strand synthesized discontinuously during replication?
choices: DNA polymerase synthesizes only in the 5′-to-3′ direction
The leading strand has no template

questions.question: In eukaryotic cells, most nuclear DNA is packaged around proteins called:
A chromosome replicated before cell division consists of two:
choices: Sister chromatids joined at a centromere
Homologous chromosomes joined at a telomere

questions.question: A gene is best described as:
choices: A DNA sequence that contributes to a functional product
A type of lipid in a membrane

questions.question: The process of making an RNA copy from a DNA template is called:
During transcription, which RNA base is used in place of thymine?
A DNA template strand has the sequence 3′-T A C G G A-5′. What mRNA sequence is transcribed?
The usual location of transcription of a nuclear gene in a eukaryotic cell is the:
Which molecule carries a codon sequence that is read during translation?
A codon consists of how many nucleotide bases?
Which RNA molecule brings a specific amino acid to a ribosome during translation?
Where does translation occur in a eukaryotic cell?
A DNA coding strand has the sequence 5′-A T G G A A T A A-3′. What is the corresponding mRNA sequence?
choices: 5′-A U G G A A U A A-3′
5′-U A C C U U A U U-3′
3′-A U G G A A U A A-5′
5′-A T G G A A T A A-3′

questions.question: Which statement about a stop codon is correct?
choices: It signals termination of translation and does not specify an amino acid
It is found only in DNA, never in mRNA

questions.question: A change in one nucleotide of a gene is generally called a:
A substitution changes a codon but not the amino acid it encodes. This is a:
A base substitution changes an amino-acid codon into a stop codon. What type of mutation is this?
A base substitution changes one codon so that a different amino acid is incorporated. This is a:
Why can insertion or deletion of one nucleotide in a coding sequence have a large effect on a protein?
choices: It can shift the reading frame of downstream codons
It always removes one whole chromosome
It changes every amino acid in the organism
It prevents DNA from pairing at every locus

questions.question: A three-base insertion within a coding sequence, away from regulatory regions, is least likely to cause which effect compared with a one-base insertion?
choices: A frameshift of all downstream codons
A possible change in protein function
A change to the encoded sequence

questions.question: A mutation in a somatic cell is most directly expected to be passed to:
choices: Descendants of that cell through cell division
No cells in the same organism

questions.question: A mutation in a cell that contributes to a gamete may be inherited by offspring because it can be:
A mutation is best described as:
choices: A normal separation of homologous chromosomes

questions.question: A chromosome-number change in which one chromosome is present in three copies is called:
A diploid cell is missing one chromosome from a homologous pair. This condition is called:
Failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate properly during cell division is called:
An allele is recessive in a simple complete-dominance model. What does that mean?
choices: Its phenotype is masked in a heterozygote
It is less common in every population
It cannot be inherited by a child

questions.question: Which statement about dominant alleles is scientifically sound?
choices: Dominance describes an allele's expression in a heterozygote, not its frequency
A dominant allele is always more common
A dominant allele is always beneficial
A dominant allele always produces a more severe trait

questions.question: Two genes on the same chromosome are more likely to be inherited together when they are:
What is the usual consequence of crossing over between two linked genes?
choices: Some gametes carry recombinant allele combinations
The genes move to a different species

questions.question: A population contains two alleles, A and a, with frequencies p and q. Under Hardy-Weinberg conditions, which relationship holds?
Under Hardy-Weinberg conditions for two alleles, which expression gives the expected frequency of heterozygotes?
If allele a has frequency q = 0.2 in a population at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, what is the expected frequency of aa individuals?
In a population at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, p = 0.7 and q = 0.3. What is the expected heterozygote frequency?
Which condition is required for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium in its basic model?
A trait influenced by many genes is described as:
Which is the most accurate description of an environmental effect on phenotype?
choices: Environment can influence how a genotype is expressed
Environment always changes the DNA sequence
Phenotype is determined only by environment

questions.question: Two individuals with the same genotype may show different phenotypes if:
choices: Their alleles become identical only at fertilization

questions.question: A person with genotype Aa has a dominant phenotype. Which conclusion is justified under complete dominance?
choices: The person carries one dominant and one recessive allele
The person must be homozygous dominant
The person cannot pass allele a to offspring
Every child must show the dominant phenotype

questions.question: A parent is heterozygous Bb and passes allele b to a child. What is the probability of passing b in any one gamete?
An individual with genotype AaBb has independently assorting genes. What is the probability that one gamete carries allele a and allele B?
For an AaBb parent with independently assorting genes, what is the probability of producing an AB gamete?

questions.question: A test cross for an individual showing a dominant phenotype uses which partner genotype?
choices: Any genotype with a dominant allele

questions.question: A person with genotype Aa has a dominant phenotype. Which conclusion is justified under complete dominance?
choices: The person carries one dominant and one recessive allele
The person must be homozygous dominant
The person cannot pass allele a to offspring
Every child must show the dominant phenotype
